A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EG-XC work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite layout changes and added appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of EG-XC and comparison methods on MD17, 3BPA, and QM9, including additional experiments in Appendices H–K.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds component ablations, learned-functional Δ-learning experiments, runtime measurements, and a physical-constraints comparison.

M1.justification: The four-component EG-XC architecture, readouts, and differentiable SCF training remain unchanged. The explicit loss, activation, and truncation descriptions add implementation information. Appendix L evaluates the Δ-learning combination already suggested in v1 Appendix I.

E1.justification: MD17, 3BPA, and QM9 coverage is retained. Appendix N adds cumulene chains CNH4, with the stated N ranging from 2 to 38, for runtime scaling; the other new analyses reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons remain, while Table 8 adds SchNet, PaiNN, and NequIP Δ-learning combinations based on learned Dick and EG-XC functionals. Figure 7 adds runtime comparisons against LDA, SCAN, B3LYP, and ωB97X. Table 9 separately introduces an evaluated Dick-versus-Nagai comparison of physical constraints.

E3.justification: Existing accuracy benchmarks retain their splits, metrics, and stated hyperparameters. New protocols include fixed-budget runtime measurements using 15 SCF cycles and 6-31G(d), plus component-removal controls, including replacement of message passing with a node-wise equivariant MLP.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled removal of the mGGA, graph readout, and GNN in Table 3. Appendices L, N, and O additionally investigate complementarity with Δ-learning, runtime scaling, and whether physical constraints improve extrapolation. These address architectural and explanatory questions absent from v1's analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix N newly reports ten repetitions per timing calculation and uses their minimum. This is a new timing aggregation practice, not evidence of increased training runs. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty or confidence intervals for the accuracy results.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark tables and QM9 heatmap preserve their numerical results. Substantial new outcomes include 300K relative MAE of 7.00 mEh without mGGA versus 0.42 for full EG-XC in Table 3, 0.29 for EG-XC-based Δ-PaiNN in Table 8, mixed Dick/Nagai rankings in Table 9, and the runtime curves in Figure 7.

T1.justification: Appendix M adds stage-by-stage asymptotic cost analysis with explicit truncation and omitted-precomputation assumptions. Appendix A inserts a missing factor of one-half in the Hartree integral expansion, and Section 5 states the twice-differentiability requirement. The underlying equivariance and SCF mathematical framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refine the contribution's scope from generic long-range interactions to atomic-range density compression and molecular-range message passing, with an explicit contrast to earlier fixed descriptors. The headline energy-only training, accuracy, and data-efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of individual component contributions, MD17 interpolation versus extrapolation, and complementarity with Δ-learning. It also explicitly identifies the need for spin information in open-shell systems and qualifies the benefits of physical constraints using the inconclusive Appendix O comparison. These substantially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link, the explicit multi-iteration energy loss, SiLU activation and differentiation details, expanded quadrature/Fock implementation explanations, and disclosure of summation truncation. Appendix N supplies timing hardware and implementation details, including a single NVIDIA A100 and density fitting for hybrid exchange. Existing hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3 remains essentially unchanged, while the abstract sharpens positioning against semi-local functionals and fixed descriptors. Hendrycks and Gimpel is newly cited; the Gasteiger et al. (2022) reference disappears, leaving unresolved citation markers in Section 4. Nagai et al. (2020) was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory method explanation are rewritten, terminology is refined, and loss and interpretation paragraphs are added. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact; Appendices L–O extend the document without reorganizing its established narrative.

P2.justification: New Tables 3, 8, and 9 and runtime Figure 7 substantially expand the displayed evidence. Existing Figures 1–6 retain their content but are repositioned or resized within the conference layout. The new ablation table incorrectly labels all three dihedral columns β = 120°, obscuring their individual identities.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential gaps in v1: Table 3 tests which architectural components matter, and Appendices M–N substantiate computational-efficiency claims with cost analysis and measurements. Expanded implementation documentation and code access improve reproducibility, while the open-shell limitation and physical-constraints analysis better qualify applicability. These gains substantially strengthen the paper despite localized new defects, especially the repeated dihedral headers and unresolved method citations.
